DataArtifactServer.definition: A data artifact server provides access services to content in a content repository.  The content repository or content store is a database of digital content with an associated set of data management, search and access methods allowing application-independent access to the content, rather like a digital library, but with the ability to store and modify content in addition to searching and retrieving. The content repository acts as the storage engine for a larger application such as a content management system or a document management system, which adds a user interface on top of the repository's application programming interface.

DataDependency.label: Data Dependency
DataDependency.definition: A Data Dependency exists when a process, operation, or system requires specific data in order to execute correctly.

DataExchangeMapping.label: Data Exchange Mapping
DataExchangeMapping.definition: Data exchange mapping identifies and models the organization's intended design for the flows of the data types, formats, and volumes between systems at the application layer.

DataInventory.label: Data Inventory
DataInventory.definition: Data inventorying identifies and records the schemas, formats, volumes, and locations of data stored and used on the organization's architecture.

DataLinkLink.label: Data Link Link
DataLinkLink.definition: A communication link between two network devices connected directly at the physical layer and on the same network segment; i.e., an OSI Layer 2 link.

Database.label: Database
Database.definition: A database is an organized collection of data, generally stored and accessed electronically from a computer system. Where databases are more complex they are often developed using formal design and modeling techniques.

DatabaseApplication.label: Database Application
DatabaseApplication.definition: A database application is a computer program whose primary purpose is retrieving information from a computerized database.

DatabaseFile.label: Database File
DatabaseFile.definition: A file that stores data and metadata in an organized format, managed by a database management system.

DatabaseQuery.label: Database Query
DatabaseQuery.definition: A specific query expressed in SQL, SPARQL, or similar language against a database.

DatabaseRecord.label: Database Record
DatabaseRecord.definition: A single, implicitly structured data item in a table in a database.

DatabaseServer.label: Database Server
DatabaseServer.definition: A database server is a server which uses a database application that provides database services to other computer programs or to computers, as defined by the client-server model. Database management systems (DBMSs) frequently provide database-server functionality, and some database management systems (such as MySQL) rely exclusively on the client-server model for database access (while others e.g. SQLite are meant for using as an embedded database). For clarification, a database server is simply a server that maintains services related to clients via database applications.

DatabaseService.label: Database Service
DatabaseService.definition: A database service interacts with a database, either retrieving data through queries or making modifications to its contents.

DatabaseServiceApplication.label: Database Service Application
DatabaseServiceApplication.definition: A software application that interacts with a database management system (DBMS) hosted as a separate, standalone service or server.

Datalog.label: Datalog
Datalog.definition: Datalog is a declarative logic programming language that is a syntactically a subset of Prolog.

DeadCodeElimination.label: Dead Code Elimination
DeadCodeElimination.definition: Removing unreachable or "dead code" from compiled source code.

Deceive.label: Deceive
Deceive.definition: The deceive tactic is used to advertise, entice, and allow potential attackers access to an observed or controlled environment.

DecisionTree.label: Decision Tree
DecisionTree.definition: Decision tree learning is a supervised learning approach used in statistics, data mining, and machine learning. In this formalism, a classification or regression decision tree is used as a predictive model to draw conclusions about a set of observations.

DecisionTreeRegression.label: Decision Tree Regression
DecisionTreeRegression.definition: Decision Trees Regression is asupervised learning method with the goal  to create a model that predicts the value of a target variable by learning simple decision rules inferred from the data features

DecoderApplication.label: Decoder Application
DecoderApplication.definition: An application that decodes digital data.

DecoyArtifact.label: Decoy Artifact
DecoyArtifact.definition: A decoy is an imitation digital artifact in any sense of a digital artifact, object, or phenomenon that is intended to deceive a cyber attacker's surveillance devices or mislead their evaluation.  Examples include fake files, accounts, hosts (honeypots), and network segments (honeynets).

DecoyEnvironment.label: Decoy Environment
DecoyEnvironment.definition: A Decoy Environment comprises hosts and networks for the purposes of deceiving an attacker.

DecoyFile.label: Decoy File
DecoyFile.definition: A file created for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

DecoyNetworkResource.label: Decoy Network Resource
DecoyNetworkResource.definition: Deploying a network resource for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

DecoyObject.label: Decoy Object
DecoyObject.definition: A Decoy Object is created and deployed for the purposes of deceiving attackers.

DecoyPersona.label: Decoy Persona
DecoyPersona.definition: Establishing a fake online identity to misdirect, deceive, and or interact with adversaries.

DecoyPublicRelease.label: Decoy Public Release
DecoyPublicRelease.definition: Issuing publicly released media to deceive adversaries.

DecoySessionToken.label: Decoy Session Token
DecoySessionToken.definition: An authentication token created for the purposes of deceiving an adversary.

DecoyUserCredential.label: Decoy User Credential
DecoyUserCredential.definition: A Credential created for the purpose of deceiving an adversary.

DeepConvolutionalGAN.label: Deep Convolutional GAN
DeepConvolutionalGAN.definition: Deep Convolutional GAN (DCGAN) uses convolutional and convolutional-transpose layers in the generator and discriminator, respectively.

DeepNeuralNetClassification.label: Deep Neural Network Classification
DeepNeuralNetClassification.definition: A deep neural network (DNN) is an artificial neural network (ANN) with multiple layers between the input and output layers. There are different types of neural networks but they always consist of the same components: neurons, synapses, weights, biases, and functions. These components as a whole function similarly to a human brain, and can be trained like any other ML algorithm

DeepQ-learning.label: Deep Q-learning
DeepQ-learning.definition: Uses a deep convolutional neural network, with layers of tiled convolutional filters to mimic the effects of receptive fields.

DefaultUserAccount.label: Default User Account
DefaultUserAccount.definition: Default accounts are those that are built-into an OS, such as the Guest or Administrator accounts on Windows systems or default factory/provider set accounts on other types of systems, software, or devices.

DefenseEvasionTechnique.label: Defense Evasion Technique
DefenseEvasionTechnique.definition: The adversary is trying to avoid being detected.

DefensiveTactic.label: Defensive Tactic
DefensiveTactic.definition: A plan for attaining a particular goal.

DefensiveTechnique.label: Defensive Technique
DefensiveTechnique.definition: A method which makes a computer system more difficult to attack.

DeleteFile.label: Delete File
DeleteFile.definition: Remove a file from a machine.

Density-basedClustering.label: Density-based Clustering
Density-basedClustering.definition: Density-based clustering connects areas of high example density into clusters. This allows for arbitrary-shaped distributions as long as dense areas can be connected.

Density-weightedMethod.label: Density-weighted Method
Density-weightedMethod.definition: An Actvie Learning technique that uses a density estimate meta-parameter to avoid sampling sparsely populated regions of the feature space and can be based parametrically or from a parameter free model.

DeonticLogic.label: Deontic Logic
DeonticLogic.definition: Deontic logic addresses the modality of obligations and norms; i.e., the modality of morality.

Dependency.label: Dependency
Dependency.definition: A dependency is the relationship of relying on or being controlled by someone or something else.  This class reifies dependencies that correspond to the object property depends-on.

DescriptionLogic.label: Description Logic
DescriptionLogic.definition: A description logic (DL) is a form of logic usually more expressive than propositional logic but less expressive than first-order logic.

DescriptiveStatistics.label: Descriptive Statistics
DescriptiveStatistics.definition: Descriptive statistics provide simple summaries about the sample and about the observations that have been made.

DeserializationFunction.label: Deserialization Function
DeserializationFunction.definition: Function with an input of serialized data which deserializes that data, usually with data parsing methods.

DesktopComputer.label: Desktop Computer
DesktopComputer.definition: A desktop computer is a personal computer designed for regular use at a single location on or near a desk or table due to its size and power requirements. The most common configuration has a case that houses the power supply, motherboard (a printed circuit board with a microprocessor as the central processing unit (CPU), memory, bus, and other electronic components, disk storage (usually one or more hard disk drives, solid state drives, optical disc drives, and in early models a floppy disk drive); a keyboard and mouse for input; and a computer monitor, speakers, and, often, a printer for output. The case may be oriented horizontally or vertically and placed either underneath, beside, or on top of a desk.

Detect.label: Detect
Detect.definition: The detect tactic is used to identify adversary access to or unauthorized activity on computer networks.

DetectionEvent.label: Detection Event
DetectionEvent.definition: An event capturing the identification of a potential security issue, such as unauthorized access attempts, policy violations, or anomalous activities. Detection events form the foundation of cybersecurity monitoring and response.

DeveloperApplication.label: Developer Application
DeveloperApplication.definition: An application used to develop computer software including applications used for software construction, analysis, testing, packaging, or management.

DialUpModem.label: Dial Up Modem
DialUpModem.definition: A dial-up modem transmits computer data over an ordinary switched telephone line that has not been designed for data use. This contrasts with leased line modems, which also operate over lines provided by a telephone company, but ones which are intended for data use and do not impose the same signaling constraints. The modulated data must fit the frequency constraints of a normal voice audio signal, and the modem must be able to perform the actions needed to connect a call through a telephone exchange, namely: picking up the line, dialing, understanding signals sent back by phone company equipment (dial tone, ringing, busy signal,) and on the far end of the call, the second modem in the connection must be able to recognize the incoming ring signal and answer the line.

DifferentialVolumeSnapshot.label: Differential Volume Snapshot
DifferentialVolumeSnapshot.definition: A differential volume snapshot is a point-in-time capture of the files and directories that were changed since the last full snapshot.

DigitalAccessBadge.label: Digital Access Badge
DigitalAccessBadge.definition: A credential used to gain entry to an area having automated access control entry points. Example media being magnetic stripe, proximity, barcode, or smart cards are examples.

DigitalArtifact.label: Digital Artifact
DigitalArtifact.definition: An information-bearing artifact (object) that is, or is encoded to be used with, a digital computer system. This concept is broad to include the literal instances of an artifact, or an implicit summarization of changes to or properties of other artifacts.

DigitalAudio.label: Digital Audio
DigitalAudio.definition: Digital audio is a representation of sound recorded in, or converted into, digital form.

DigitalAudioVisualMedia.label: Digital Audio Visual Media
DigitalAudioVisualMedia.definition: Audiovisual (AV) is electronic media possessing both a sound and a visual component.

DigitalCamera.label: Digital Camera
DigitalCamera.definition: An optical instrument that can capture an image. A digital camera that captures photographs in digital memory.

DigitalDocument.label: Digital Document
DigitalDocument.definition: An digital document is any electronic media content (other than computer programs or system files) that is intended to be used in either an electronic form or as printed output.

DigitalEvent.label: Digital Event
DigitalEvent.definition: A digital event represents an observable occurrence, action, or state change within digital systems, networks, or their interactions. These events are characterized by their impact on the confidentiality, integrity, availability, or functionality of digital resources, processes, identities, or communications. Digital events are essential units of information in cybersecurity, serving as the basis for detecting threats, analyzing anomalies, and orchestrating responses in complex, interconnected environments.

DigitalEventRecord.label: Digital Event Record
DigitalEventRecord.definition: A digital event record is a structured representation of a digital event, encapsulating all relevant details about the occurrence for storage, analysis, and response. These records serve as the primary artifacts for cybersecurity operations, enabling threat detection, forensic investigations, and compliance reporting. Digital event records include metadata such as timestamps, origin, context, and associated resources, ensuring traceability and actionable intelligence in digital ecosystems.

DigitalFingerprint.label: Digital Fingerprint
DigitalFingerprint.definition: A digital signature uniquely identifies data and has the property that changing a single bit in the data will cause a completely different message digest to be generated.

DigitalIdentity.label: Digital Identity
DigitalIdentity.definition: The unique representation of a subject engaged in an online transaction. A digital identity is always unique in the context of a digital service, but does not necessarily need to uniquely identify the subject in all contexts. In other words, accessing a digital service may not mean that the subject's real-life identity is known.  Note: There is no single, widely accepted definition for this term and context is important. This definition is specific to online transactions.

DigitalImage.label: Digital Image
DigitalImage.definition: A digital image is a pixel-based visual representation stored in formats like JPEG or PNG, used for various digital applications.

DigitalInformation.label: Digital Information
DigitalInformation.definition: Digital information is a broad category of encoded representations in digital form that convey meaning, instructions, or functionality.

DigitalInformationBearer.label: Digital Information Bearer
DigitalInformationBearer.definition: A digital information bearer is a physical or virtual entity that stores, transmits, or processes digital information.

DigitalMedia.label: Digital Media
DigitalMedia.definition: Digital media refers to any communication media that operate in conjunction with various encoded machine-readable data formats.

DigitalMessage.label: Digital Message
DigitalMessage.definition: A discrete unit of digital communication created by a sender for one or more intended recipients. Encoded in an application-layer format, a digital message conveys semantics such as commands, data, or status and is transported inside lower-layer containers like network frames or packets.

DigitalMultimedia.label: Digital Multimedia
DigitalMultimedia.definition: Digital Multimedia refers to content that combines text, audio, images, animations, and video in a digital format for interactive applications.

DigitalSignalProcessingApplication.label: Digital Signal Processing Application
DigitalSignalProcessingApplication.definition: A Digital Signal Processing (DSP) application is a software system that ingests discrete-time or discrete-space signals (from sensors, ADCs, or files) and applies digital signal processing algorithms to analyze, transform, synthesize, or make decisions about those signals, often under real-time throughput and latency constraints. It encompasses capabilities such as filtering, spectral analysis, modulation/demodulation, channelization, synchronization, detection and estimation, compression, beamforming, and reconstruction, and spans domains including software-defined radio (e.g., waveform generation and physical-layer stacks), audio and speech, image and video, radar/sonar/LiDAR, biomedical signals, instrumentation, and control.

DigitalSystem.label: Digital System
DigitalSystem.definition: A digital system is a group of interacting or interrelated digital artifacts that act according to a set of rules to form a unified whole. A digital system, surrounded and influenced by its environment, is described by its boundaries, structure and purpose and expressed in its functioning. Systems are the subjects of study of systems theory.

DigitalText.label: Digital Text
DigitalText.definition: Digital text is written content encoded in a digital format, allowing for storage, retrieval, and manipulation by electronic devices.

DigitalVideo.label: Digital Video
DigitalVideo.definition: Digital video is an electronic representation of moving visual images (video) in the form of encoded digital data.

DimensionReduction.label: Dimension Reduction
DimensionReduction.definition: Dimensionality reduction is a key technique within unsupervised learning. It compresses the data by finding a smaller, different set of variables that capture what matters most in the original features, while minimizing the loss of information.

DirectPhysicalLinkMapping.label: Direct Physical Link Mapping
DirectPhysicalLinkMapping.definition: Direct physical link mapping creates a physical link map by direct observation and recording of the physical network links.

DirectionalNetworkLink.label: Directional Network Link
DirectionalNetworkLink.definition: Enforce one-way network communication by preventing two-way communication.

Directory.label: Directory
Directory.definition: In computing, a directory is a file system cataloging structure which contains references to other computer files, and possibly other directories. On many computers, directories are known as folders, or drawers to provide some relevancy to a workbench or the traditional office file cabinet.

DirectoryService.label: Directory Service
DirectoryService.definition: In computing, directory service or name service maps the names of network resources to their respective network addresses. It is a shared information infrastructure for locating, managing, administering and organizing everyday items and network resources, which can include volumes, folders, files, printers, users, groups, devices, telephone numbers and other objects. A directory service is a critical component of a network operating system. A directory server or name server is a server which provides such a service. Each resource on the network is considered an object by the directory server. Information about a particular resource is stored as a collection of attributes associated with that resource or object.

DisableRemoteAccess.label: Disable Remote Access
DisableRemoteAccess.definition: Limiting access to a computing device which is not required through or from a non-organization-controlled network.

DiscoveryTechnique.label: Discovery Technique
DiscoveryTechnique.definition: The adversary is trying to figure out your environment.

DiscriminantAnalysis.label: Discriminant Analysis
DiscriminantAnalysis.definition: Discriminant analysis attempts to establish whether a set of variables can be used to distinguish between two or more groups of cases.

DiskEncryption.label: Disk Encryption
DiskEncryption.definition: Encrypting a hard disk partition to prevent cleartext access to a file system.

DiskErasure.label: Disk Erasure
DiskErasure.definition: Disk Erasure is the process of securely deleting all data on a disk to ensure that it cannot be recovered by any means.

DiskFormatting.label: Disk Formatting
DiskFormatting.definition: Disk Formatting is the process of preparing a data storage device, such as a hard drive, solid-state drive, or USB flash drive, for initial use.

DiskImage.label: Disk Image
DiskImage.definition: A disk image is a snapshot of a storage device's structure and data typically stored in one or more computer files on another storage device.

DiskPartitioning.label: Disk Partitioning
DiskPartitioning.definition: Disk Partitioning is the process of dividing a disk into multiple distinct sections, known as partitions.

DisplayAdapter.label: Display Adapter
DisplayAdapter.definition: A graphics card (also called a display card, video card, display adapter, or graphics adapter) is an expansion card which generates a feed of output images to a display device (such as a computer monitor). Frequently, these are advertised as discrete or dedicated graphics cards, emphasizing the distinction between these and integrated graphics. At the core of both is the graphics processing unit (GPU), which is the main part that does the actual computations, but should not be confused with the video card as a whole, although "GPU" is often used to refer to video cards.

DisplayDeviceDriver.label: Display Device Driver
DisplayDeviceDriver.definition: A device driver for a display adapter.

DisplayServer.label: Display Server
DisplayServer.definition: A display server or window server is a program whose primary task is to coordinate the input and output of its clients to and from the rest of the operating system, the hardware, and each other. The display server communicates with its clients over the display server protocol, a communications protocol, which can be network-transparent or simply network-capable. The display server is a key component in any graphical user interface, specifically the windowing system.

Distribution-basedClustering.label: Distribution-based Clustering
Distribution-basedClustering.definition: Distribution-based clustering creates and groups data points based on their likely hood of belonging to the same probability distribution (Gaussian, Binomial, etc.) in the data.

DistributionProperties.label: Distribution Properties
DistributionProperties.definition: The properties derived from a probability distribution.

DivisiveClustering.label: Divisive Clustering
DivisiveClustering.definition: A divisive clustering approach is a hierarchical, top-down approach to clustering a dataset.

DocumentFile.label: Document File
DocumentFile.definition: A document is a written, drawn, presented or recorded representation of thoughts. An electronic document file is usually used to describe a primarily textual file, along with its structure and design, such as fonts, colors and additional images.

DomainAccountMonitoring.label: Domain Account Monitoring
DomainAccountMonitoring.definition: Monitoring the existence of or changes to Domain User Accounts.

DomainLogicValidation.label: Domain Logic Validation
DomainLogicValidation.definition: Validation of variable state in the context of the domain application.

DomainName.label: Domain Name
DomainName.definition: A domain name is an identification string that defines a realm of administrative autonomy, authority or control within the Internet. Domain names are formed by the rules and procedures of the Domain Name System (DNS). Any name registered in the DNS is a domain name.Domain names are used in various networking contexts and application-specific naming and addressing purposes. In general, a domain name represents an Internet Protocol (IP) resource, such as a personal computer used to access the Internet, a server computer hosting a web site, or the web site itself or any other service communicated via the Internet. In 2015, 294 million domain names had been registered.

DomainNameReputationAnalysis.label: Domain Name Reputation Analysis
DomainNameReputationAnalysis.definition: Analyzing the reputation of a domain name.

DomainRegistration.label: Domain Registration
DomainRegistration.definition: A domain registration, or domain name registration data, is the relevant registration data from Internet resources such as domain names, IP addresses, and autonomous system numbers. Registration data is typically retrieved by means of either the Registration Data Access Protocol (RDAP) or its predecessor, the WHOIS protocol.

DomainRegistrationTakedown.label: Domain Registration Takedown
DomainRegistrationTakedown.definition: The process of performing a takedown of the attacker's domain registration infrastructure.

DomainTrustPolicy.label: Domain Trust Policy
DomainTrustPolicy.definition: Restricting inter-domain trust by modifying domain configuration.

DomainUserAccount.label: Domain User Account
DomainUserAccount.definition: A domain user account in Microsoft Windows (2000) defines that user's access to a logical group of network objects (computers, users, devices) that share the same Active Directory databases; that is, a user's access to a domain.

DriverLoadIntegrityChecking.label: Driver Load Integrity Checking
DriverLoadIntegrityChecking.definition: Ensuring the integrity of drivers loaded during initialization of the operating system.

Dyna-Q.label: Dyna-Q
Dyna-Q.definition: A Dyna-Q agent combines acting, learning, and planning.

DynamicAnalysis.label: Dynamic Analysis
DynamicAnalysis.definition: Executing or opening a file in a synthetic "sandbox" environment to determine if the file is a malicious program or if the file exploits another program such as a document reader.

DynamicAnalysisTool.label: Dynamic Analysis Tool
DynamicAnalysisTool.definition: Dynamic program analysis is the analysis of computer software that is performed by executing programs on a real or virtual processor.

ElectricalSignal.label: Electrical Signal
ElectricalSignal.definition: Time-varying voltage or current that carries information.

ElectromagneticRadiationHardening.label: Electromagnetic Radiation Hardening
ElectromagneticRadiationHardening.definition: The application of physical and material-level design measures to electronic systems, components, or facilities to reduce their susceptibility to damage or disruption from electromagnetic threats.

ElectromagneticSignal.label: Electromagnetic Signal
ElectromagneticSignal.definition: An electromagnetic wave that carries information.

ElectronicCombinationLock.label: Electronic Combination Lock
ElectronicCombinationLock.definition: A system comprised of an automatic door closer on the door, an input device, a controlling device, and a lock, usually mechanical, which is released or activated when the correct combination is entered or correct token is presented.

ElectronicCombinationLockEvent.label: Electronic Combination Lock Event
ElectronicCombinationLockEvent.definition: An event occuring when combination lock's bolt changes position.

ElectronicLockMonitoring.label: Electronic Lock Monitoring
ElectronicLockMonitoring.definition: Monitoring electronic lock and door hardware states and access events (e.g., locked/unlocked, access granted/denied, door forced/held, tamper) to detect and respond to unauthorized entry.

Email.label: Email
Email.definition: An email, or email message, is a document that is sent between computer users across computer networks.

EmailAttachment.label: Email Attachment
EmailAttachment.definition: An email attachment is a computer file sent along with an email message. One or more files can be attached to any email message, and be sent along with it to the recipient. This is typically used as a simple method to share documents and images.

EmailEvent.label: Email Event
EmailEvent.definition: An event involving email communication, including sending, receiving, and processing emails. Email events encapsulate activities essential to the transmission and analysis of email messages in a networked environment.

EmailFiltering.label: Email Filtering
EmailFiltering.definition: Filtering incoming email traffic based on specific criteria.

EmailReceiveEvent.label: Email Receive Event
EmailReceiveEvent.definition: An event where an email is delivered to a recipient's mail server or mailbox. This includes receiving messages from internal or external sources via protocols such as IMAP, POP3, or their secure variants.

EmailRemoval.label: Email Removal
EmailRemoval.definition: The email removal technique deletes email files from system storage.

EmailRule.label: Email Rule
EmailRule.definition: A configuration of an email application which is used to apply logical or data processing functions to data processed by the email  application.

EmailScanEvent.label: Email Scan Event
EmailScanEvent.definition: An event where an email is inspected or analyzed for content, security, or compliance purposes. Scanning often involves identifying spam, detecting malware, or ensuring policy adherence before delivery or after reception.

EmailSendEvent.label: Email Send Event
EmailSendEvent.definition: An event where an email is transmitted from a client to a recipient via a mail server. This process often involves protocols such as SMTP or its secure variants, with potential authentication and encryption for secure delivery.

EmbeddedComputer.label: Embedded Computer
EmbeddedComputer.definition: An embedded computer is a computer system -- a combination of a computer processor, computer memory, and input/output peripheral devices-that has a dedicated function within a larger mechanical or electrical system. It is embedded as part of a complete device often including electrical or electronic hardware and mechanical parts. Because an embedded system typically controls physical operations of the machine that it is embedded within, it often has real-time computing constraints. Embedded systems control many devices in common use today. Ninety-eight percent of all microprocessors manufactured are used in embedded systems.

EmbeddedDatabaseApplication.label: Embedded Database Application
EmbeddedDatabaseApplication.definition: A software application that integrates a database management system (DBMS) directly within its own structure, rather than relying on a separate, standalone database server. Examples include SQLite and Berkeley DB.

EmulatedFileAnalysis.label: Emulated File Analysis
EmulatedFileAnalysis.definition: Emulating instructions in a file looking for specific patterns.

Enclave.label: Enclave
Enclave.definition: Network enclaves consist of standalone assets that do not interact with other information systems or networks. A major difference between a DMZ or demilitarized zone and a network enclave is a DMZ allows inbound and outbound traffic access, where firewall boundaries are traversed. In an enclave, firewall boundaries are not traversed. Enclave protection tools can be used to provide protection within specific security domains. These mechanisms are installed as part of an Intranet to connect networks that have similar security requirements.

EncoderApplication.label: Encoder Application
EncoderApplication.definition: An application that encodes digital data.

EncryptedTunnels.label: Encrypted Tunnels
EncryptedTunnels.definition: Encrypted encapsulation of routable network traffic.

Endpoint-basedWebServerAccessMediation.label: Endpoint-based Web Server Access Mediation
Endpoint-basedWebServerAccessMediation.definition: Endpoint-based web server access mediation regulates web server access directly from user endpoints by implementing mechanisms such as client-side certificates and endpoint security software to authenticate devices and ensure compliant access.

EndpointHealthBeacon.label: Endpoint Health Beacon
EndpointHealthBeacon.definition: Monitoring the security status of an endpoint by sending periodic messages with health status, where absence of a response may indicate that the endpoint has been compromised.

EndpointSensor.label: Endpoint Sensor
EndpointSensor.definition: A sensor application installed on a endpoint (platform) to collect information on platform components.

EnsembleLearning.label: Ensemble Learning
EnsembleLearning.definition: In statistics and machine learning, ensemble methods use multiple learning algorithms to obtain better predictive performance than could be obtained from any of the constituent learning algorithms alone

EpistemicLogic.label: Epistemic Logic
EpistemicLogic.definition: Epistemic logic addresses modalities of knowledge; i.e., the certainty of sentences.

EquivalenceMatching.label: Equivalence Matching
EquivalenceMatching.definition: Equivalence matching is matching two values, which may be bound to variables, to see if they are equivalent.

Estimation.label: Estimation
Estimation.definition: Estimation represents ways or a process of learning and determining the population parameter based on the model fitted to the data.

EvalFunction.label: Eval Function
EvalFunction.definition: Takes inputs of strings and evaluations them as expressions.

Event.label: Event
Event.definition: An Event is an occurrence or action within a system, process, or environment within a finite span of time.

EventLog.label: Event Log
EventLog.definition: Event logs record events taking place in the execution of a system in order to provide an audit trail that can be used to understand the activity of the system and to diagnose problems. They are essential to understand the activities of complex systems, particularly in the case of applications with little user interaction (such as server applications).

EventLogArchiveEvent.label: Event Log Archive Event
EventLogArchiveEvent.definition: An event involving the archiving of event log data, typically to preserve historical records in a compressed or secure format.

EventLogClearEvent.label: Event Log Clear Event
EventLogClearEvent.definition: An event where the event log data is cleared from the system, often as part of log maintenance or potentially to cover tracks.

EventLogDeleteEvent.label: Event Log Delete Event
EventLogDeleteEvent.definition: An event where the event log database, file, or cache is deleted from the system, removing the log's historical records.

EventLogDisableEvent.label: Event Log Disable Event
EventLogDisableEvent.definition: An event indicating that the event logging service has been disabled, preventing it from collecting or recording logs.

EventLogEnableEvent.label: Event Log Enable Event
EventLogEnableEvent.definition: An event where the event logging service is enabled, allowing it to actively collect and record logs.

EventLogEvent.label: Event Log Event
EventLogEvent.definition: An event that captures actions or operations related to the management of system event logs, including modifications, access, and service state changes.

EventLogExportEvent.label: Event Log Export Event
EventLogExportEvent.definition: An event representing the export of event log data to a file or external system for backup or analysis purposes.

EventLogRestartEvent.label: Event Log Restart Event
EventLogRestartEvent.definition: An event representing the restarting of the event logging service, often performed during system maintenance or troubleshooting.

EventLogRotateEvent.label: Event Log Rotate Event
EventLogRotateEvent.definition: An event where the event log is rotated, often as part of log rotation policies to manage storage and ensure continuity.

EventLogStartEvent.label: Event Log Start Event
EventLogStartEvent.definition: An event where the event logging service is started, enabling the collection and recording of system events.

EventLogStopEvent.label: Event Log Stop Event
EventLogStopEvent.definition: An event indicating that the event logging service has been stopped, halting the recording of system events.

Evict.label: Evict
Evict.definition: The eviction tactic is used to remove an adversary from a computer network.

EvictionEvent.label: Eviction Event
EvictionEvent.definition: An event describing actions to remove adversaries or malicious resources from a system, re-establishing security and operational integrity.

ExactMatching.label: Exact Matching
ExactMatching.definition: Exact matching for numeric types is just the simple test for mathematical equivalence of the values being matched.

ExceptionHandler.label: Exception Handler
ExceptionHandler.definition: An exception handler is a code segment that processes an exception.

ExceptionHandlerPointerValidation.label: Exception Handler Pointer Validation
ExceptionHandlerPointerValidation.definition: Validates that a referenced exception handler pointer is a valid exception handler.

ExecutableAllowlisting.label: Executable Allowlisting
ExecutableAllowlisting.definition: Using a digital signature to authenticate a file before opening.

ExecutableBinary.label: Executable Binary
ExecutableBinary.definition: An executable binary contains machine code instructions for a physical CPU. D3FEND also considers byte code for a virtual machine to be binary code.  This is in contrast to executable scripts written in a scripting language.

ExecutableDenylisting.label: Executable Denylisting
ExecutableDenylisting.definition: Blocking the execution of files on a host in accordance with defined application policy rules.

ExecutableFile.label: Executable File
ExecutableFile.definition: In computing, executable code or an executable file or executable program, sometimes simply an executable, causes a computer "to perform indicated tasks according to encoded instructions," as opposed to a data file that must be parsed by a program to be meaningful. These instructions are traditionally machine code instructions for a physical CPU. However, in a more general sense, a file containing instructions (such as bytecode) for a software interpreter may also be considered executable; even a scripting language source file may therefore be considered executable in this sense. The exact interpretation depends upon the use; while the term often refers only to machine code files, in the context of protection against computer viruses all files which cause potentially hazardous instruction

ExecutableScript.label: Executable Script
ExecutableScript.definition: An executable script is written in a scripting language and interpreted at run time. This is in contrast with an executable binary, which contains machine code instructions for a physical CPU or byte code for a virtual machine.

ExecutionIsolation.label: Execution Isolation
ExecutionIsolation.definition: Execution Isolation techniques prevent application processes from accessing non-essential system resources, such as memory, devices, or files.

ExecutionTechnique.label: Execution Technique
ExecutionTechnique.definition: The adversary is trying to run malicious code.

ExfiltrationTechnique.label: Exfiltration Technique
ExfiltrationTechnique.definition: The adversary is trying to steal data.

Expectation-maximizationClustering.label: Expectation-maximization Clustering
Expectation-maximizationClustering.definition: An unsupervised clustering algorithm and extends to NLP applications like Latent Dirichlet Allocation, the Baum-Welch algorithm for Hidden Markov Models, and medical imaging.

ExpectedErrorReduction.label: Expected Error Reduction
ExpectedErrorReduction.definition: Expected Error Reduction (EER) follows similar ideas as EMC, but again looks at the model output instead of the model itself and also takes the other data into account. In particular, a sample x is considered useful, if we can expect that knowing the label will reduce the future error on unseen samples

ExpectedModelChange.label: Expected Model Change
ExpectedModelChange.definition: Supervised learning establishes a relationship between the known input and output variables to conduct a predictive analysis.

ExternalContentInclusionFunction.label: External Content Inclusion Function
ExternalContentInclusionFunction.definition: A subroutine which handles a content inclusion directive from an original file. When invoked, the external content is included in the resulting open file.

FPGABitstream.label: FPGA Bitstream
FPGABitstream.definition: A binary configuration file generated by synthesizing and placing-and-routing an HDL design, which is loaded into a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) to physically define its internal logic, interconnects, and I/O behavior. Rather than being executed by a processor, it programs the device itself.

FTPDeleteEvent.label: FTP Delete Event
FTPDeleteEvent.definition: An event where files or directories are removed from an FTP server, resulting in their permanent deletion from the remote system.

FTPEvent.label: FTP Event
FTPEvent.definition: An event involving the File Transfer Protocol (FTP), a standard network protocol used to transfer files between a client and server over a TCP/IP network. FTP facilitates operations such as file uploads, downloads, directory listing, and remote file management.

FTPGetEvent.label: FTP Get Event
FTPGetEvent.definition: An event where a file is downloaded from an FTP server to a client, retrieving data from the remote system to the local destination.

FTPListEvent.label: FTP List Event
FTPListEvent.definition: An event where the contents of a directory on an FTP server are listed, providing metadata such as file names, sizes, and timestamps.

FTPPollEvent.label: FTP Poll Event
FTPPollEvent.definition: An event where a client queries an FTP server to check for the presence of specific files or directories without initiating a transfer.

FTPPutEvent.label: FTP Put Event
FTPPutEvent.definition: An event where a file is uploaded from a client to an FTP server, transferring data from the local system to the remote destination.

FTPRenameEvent.label: FTP Rename Event
FTPRenameEvent.definition: An event where files or directories on an FTP server are renamed, modifying their identifiers without altering their content or location.

FastSymbolicLink.label: Fast Symbolic Link
FastSymbolicLink.definition: Fast symbolic links, allow storage of the target path within the data structures used for storing file information on disk (e.g., within the inodes). This space normally stores a list of disk block addresses allocated to a file. Thus, symlinks with short target paths are accessed quickly. Systems with fast symlinks often fall back to using the original method if the target path exceeds the available inode space.

File.label: File
File.definition: A file maintained in computer-readable form.

FileAccessEvent.label: File Access Event
FileAccessEvent.definition: An event where a file is accessed for operations such as reading, opening, or inspecting its contents or metadata, without necessarily modifying its state.

FileAccessPatternAnalysis.label: File Access Pattern Analysis
FileAccessPatternAnalysis.definition: Analyzing the files accessed by a process to identify unauthorized activity.

FileAnalysis.label: File Analysis
FileAnalysis.definition: File Analysis is an analytic process to determine a file's status. For example: virus, trojan, benign, malicious, trusted, unauthorized, sensitive, etc.

FileCarving.label: File Carving
FileCarving.definition: Identifying and extracting files from network application protocols through the use of network stream reassembly software.

FileContentAnalysis.label: File Content Analysis
FileContentAnalysis.definition: Employing a pattern matching algorithm to statically analyze the content of files.

FileContentBlock.label: File Content Block
FileContentBlock.definition: A section within a file that contains the main content or data payload.

FileContentBlockData.label: File Content Block Data
FileContentBlockData.definition: The actual content or main data within a file or data block.

FileContentBlockMetadata.label: File Content Block Metadata
FileContentBlockMetadata.definition: Content Blocks may contain metadata specific to the block's content at the beginning.

FileContentDecompressionChecking.label: File Content Decompression Checking
FileContentDecompressionChecking.definition: Checking if compressed or encoded data sections can be successfully decompressed or decoded. Can follow with further analysis with semantic knowledge

FileContentRules.label: File Content Rules
FileContentRules.definition: Employing a pattern matching rule language to analyze the content of files.

FileCopyEvent.label: File Copy Event
FileCopyEvent.definition: An event where a file is duplicated, creating a new file in a different location or under a different name while preserving the original file's content and attributes.

FileCreationAnalysis.label: File Creation Analysis
FileCreationAnalysis.definition: Analyzing the properties of file create system call invocations.

FileCreationEvent.label: File Creation Event
FileCreationEvent.definition: An event representing the creation of a new file within the system, establishing its existence and initial attributes in the file system or storage medium.

FileDecryptionEvent.label: File Decryption Event
FileDecryptionEvent.definition: An event where a previously encrypted file is decoded, rendering its content accessible to authorized users or processes.

FileDeletionEvent.label: File Deletion Event
FileDeletionEvent.definition: An event where a file is permanently removed from the file system or storage medium, potentially triggering actions related to data retention or recovery.

FileEncryption.label: File Encryption
FileEncryption.definition: Encrypting a file using a cryptographic key.

FileEncryptionEvent.label: File Encryption Event
FileEncryptionEvent.definition: An event involving the application of cryptographic techniques to a file, ensuring its content is securely encoded and inaccessible without proper decryption keys.

FileEvent.label: File Event
FileEvent.definition: An event involving operations performed on digital files, encompassing actions such as creation, modification, deletion, access, and attribute or permission changes.

FileEviction.label: File Eviction
FileEviction.definition: File eviction techniques delete files from system storage.

FileFooterBlock.label: File Footer Block
FileFooterBlock.definition: A section at the end of a file that contains metadata or control information.

FileFooterBlockContent.label: File Footer Block Content
FileFooterBlockContent.definition: The content of a footer block not including the signature.

FileFooterBlockSignature.label: File Footer Block Signature
FileFooterBlockSignature.definition: A sequence of bytes used to identify and validate the footer section within a file.

FileFormatVerification.label: File Format Verification
FileFormatVerification.definition: Verifying that a file conforms to its expected format specifications

FileGetAttributesEvent.label: File Get Attributes Event
FileGetAttributesEvent.definition: An event where a file's metadata attributes, such as size, creation date, or type, are queried or retrieved without altering its content.

FileGetPermissionsEvent.label: File Get Permissions Event
FileGetPermissionsEvent.definition: An event where a file's security settings or access control list (ACL) is retrieved, detailing permissions granted to users or processes.

FileHash.label: File Hash
FileHash.definition: A File Hash is a fixed-length, unique digital fingerprint generated by applying a cryptographic hash function to the contents of a file.

FileHashReputationAnalysis.label: File Hash Reputation Analysis
FileHashReputationAnalysis.definition: Analyzing the reputation of a file hash.

FileHashing.label: File Hashing
FileHashing.definition: Employing file hash comparisons to detect known malware.

FileHeaderBlock.label: File Header Block
FileHeaderBlock.definition: Headers are sections of a file that organize and provide information about specific sections or components of the file. Typically found at the beginning of a file, they often contain file type identification, version information, and metadata such as size, format, and encoding.

FileHeaderBlockContent.label: File Header Block Content
FileHeaderBlockContent.definition: The content of a header block not including the signature.

FileHeaderBlockSignature.label: File Header Block Signature
FileHeaderBlockSignature.definition: A sequence of bytes used to identify and validate specific header sections within a file.

FileIntegrityMonitoring.label: File Integrity Monitoring
FileIntegrityMonitoring.definition: Detecting any suspicious changes to files in a computer system.

FileInternalStructureVerification.label: File Internal Structure Verification
FileInternalStructureVerification.definition: The process of checking specific static values within a file, such as file signatures or magic numbers, to ensure they match the expected values defined by the file format specification.

FileMagicByteVerification.label: File Magic Byte Verification
FileMagicByteVerification.definition: Utilizing the magic number to verify the file

FileMagicBytes.label: File Magic Bytes
FileMagicBytes.definition: A specific type of header signature located at the beginning of a file, used to identify the file format.

FileMetadata.label: File Metadata
FileMetadata.definition: Information that describes and provides context about a file's content, structure, and attributes.

FileMetadataConsistencyValidation.label: File Metadata Consistency Validation
FileMetadataConsistencyValidation.definition: The process of validating the consistency between a file's metadata and its actual content, ensuring that elements like declared lengths, pointers, and checksums accurately describe the file's content.

FileMetadataValueVerification.label: File Metadata Value Verification
FileMetadataValueVerification.definition: The process of checking specific static values within a file, such as file signatures or magic numbers, to ensure they match the expected values defined by the file format specification.

FileMountEvent.label: File Mount Event
FileMountEvent.definition: An event where a file system or storage volume is mounted, making its files and directories accessible to the operating system or applications.

FilePathOpenFunction.label: File Path Open Function
FilePathOpenFunction.definition: Has an input of a file path, and opens a file handle for reading or writing.

FileRenamingEvent.label: File Renaming Event
FileRenamingEvent.definition: An event representing the renaming of a file, modifying its identifier within the file system while retaining its content and metadata.

FileSection.label: File Section
FileSection.definition: A file section is one of the portions of a file in which the file is regarded as divided and where together the file sections constitute the whole file.

FileServer.label: File Server
FileServer.definition: The term server highlights the role of the machine in the traditional client-server scheme, where the clients are the workstations using the storage. A file server does not normally perform computational tasks or run programs on behalf of its client workstations. File servers are commonly found in schools and offices, where users use a local area network to connect their client computers.

FileSetAttributesEvent.label: File Set Attributes Event
FileSetAttributesEvent.definition: An event where a file's metadata attributes are modified, such as changing its timestamps, labels, or categorization within the system.

FileSetPermissionsEvent.label: File Set Permissions Event
FileSetPermissionsEvent.definition: An event involving the modification of a file's permissions or access control list (ACL), specifying which users or processes are granted or restricted access.

FileShareService.label: File Share Service
FileShareService.definition: A file sharing service (or file share service) provides the ability to share data across a network.

FileSystem.label: File System
FileSystem.definition: In computing, a file system or filesystem is used to control how data is stored and retrieved. Without a file system, information placed in a storage medium would be one large body of data with no way to tell where one piece of information stops and the next begins. By separating the data into pieces and giving each piece a name, the information is easily isolated and identified. Taking its name from the way paper-based information systems are named, each group of data is called a "file". The structure and logic rules used to manage the groups of information and their names is called a "file system".

FileSystemLink.label: File System Link
FileSystemLink.definition: A file system link associates a name with a file on a file system.  Most generally, this may be a direct reference (a hard link) or an indirect one (a soft link).

FileSystemMetadata.label: File System Metadata
FileSystemMetadata.definition: Metadata about the files and directories in a file system.  For example file name, file length, time modified, group and user ids, and other file attributes.

FileSystemSensor.label: File System Sensor
FileSystemSensor.definition: Collects files and file metadata on an endpoint.

FileTransferNetworkTraffic.label: File Transfer Network Traffic
FileTransferNetworkTraffic.definition: File transfer network traffic is network traffic related to file transfers between network nodes. This includes only network traffic conforming to standard file transfer protocols, not custom transfer protocols.

FileUnmountEvent.label: File Unmount Event
FileUnmountEvent.definition: An event where a file system or storage volume is unmounted, disconnecting its files and directories from the operating system or applications.

FileUpdateEvent.label: File Update Event
FileUpdateEvent.definition: An event involving changes to the content or metadata of an existing file, reflecting updates that alter its state or properties.

FingerPrintScannerInputDevice.label: Finger Print Scanner Input Device
FingerPrintScannerInputDevice.definition: A fingerprint sensor is an electronic device used to capture a digital image of the fingerprint pattern. The captured image is called a live scan. This live scan is digitally processed to create a biometric template (a collection of extracted features) which is stored and used for matching. Many technologies have been used including optical, capacitive, RF, thermal, piezoresistive, ultrasonic, piezoelectric, and MEMS.

Firewall.label: Firewall
Firewall.definition: In computing, a firewall is a network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules. A firewall typically establishes a barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external network, such as the Internet. Firewalls are often categorized as either network firewalls or host-based firewalls. Network firewalls filter traffic between two or more networks and run on network hardware. Host-based firewalls run on host computers and control network traffic in and out of those machines. This definition refers to network firewalls.

Firmware.label: Firmware
Firmware.definition: In electronic systems and computing, firmware is a type of software that provides control, monitoring and data manipulation of engineered products and systems. Typical examples of devices containing firmware are embedded systems (such as traffic lights, consumer appliances, remote controls and digital watches), computers, computer peripherals, mobile phones, and digital cameras. The firmware contained in these devices provides the low-level control program for the device.

FirmwareBehaviorAnalysis.label: Firmware Behavior Analysis
FirmwareBehaviorAnalysis.definition: Analyzing the behavior of embedded code in firmware and looking for anomalous behavior and suspicious activity.

FirmwareEmbeddedMonitoringCode.label: Firmware Embedded Monitoring Code
FirmwareEmbeddedMonitoringCode.definition: Monitoring code is injected into firmware for integrity monitoring of firmware and firmware data.

FirmwareSensor.label: Firmware Sensor
FirmwareSensor.definition: Collects information on firmware installed on an Endpoint.

First-orderLogic.label: First-order Logic
First-orderLogic.definition: First-order logic is a collection of formal systems used in mathematics, philosophy, linguistics, and computer science. First-order logic uses quantified variables over non-logical objects, and allows the use of sentences that contain variables.

First-stageBootLoader.label: First-stage Boot Loader
First-stageBootLoader.definition: The very first routine run in order to load the operating system.

FlashMemory.label: Flash Memory
FlashMemory.definition: Flash memory is an electronic non-volatile computer memory storage medium that can be electrically erased and reprogrammed.

ForwardProxyServer.label: Forward Proxy Server
ForwardProxyServer.definition: An forward (or open) proxy is a proxy server that is accessible by any Internet user. Generally, a proxy server only allows users within a network group (i.e. a closed proxy) to store and forward Internet services such as DNS or web pages to reduce and control the bandwidth used by the group. With an open proxy, however, any user on the Internet is able to use this forwarding service.

ForwardResolutionDomainDenylisting.label: Forward Resolution Domain Denylisting
ForwardResolutionDomainDenylisting.definition: Blocking a lookup based on the query's domain name value.

ForwardResolutionIPDenylisting.label: Forward Resolution IP Denylisting
ForwardResolutionIPDenylisting.definition: Blocking a DNS lookup's answer's IP address value.

FullVolumeSnapshot.label: Full Volume Snapshot
FullVolumeSnapshot.definition: A full volume snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the complete contents of a volume.

FuzzyLogic.label: Fuzzy Logic
FuzzyLogic.definition: Fuzzy logic is a form of many-valued logic in which the truth value of variables may be any real number between 0 and 1.

GNSSReceiver.label: GNSS Receiver
GNSSReceiver.definition: A GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) receiver is an electronic device that picks up signals from one or more satellite constellations (like GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou) to calculate precise location, velocity, and time.

GNSSSatellite.label: GNSS Satellite
GNSSSatellite.definition: A GNSS satellite is part of a space-based constellation that transmits signals, allowing receivers on Earth to determine their position, navigation, and timing (PNT) through trilateration.

GNSSSignal.label: GNSS Signal
GNSSSignal.definition: A GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) signal is a low-power radio signal broadcast from satellites that contains a carrier wave, a ranging code, and a navigation message. The receiver uses the carrier wave to precisely measure the time it takes for the signal to travel from the satellite, while the navigation message provides essential information like the satellite's position (ephemeris) and clock information.

GNSSTimeRecord.label: GNSS Time Record
GNSSTimeRecord.definition: A GNSS Time Record is an information content entity encoded in a GNSS signal that represents the transmission time of that signal as determined by the transmitting satellite, expressed relative to a constellation-specific time standard and epoch.

GPT.label: GPT
GPT.definition: Generative pre-trained transformers (GPT) are a type of large language model (LLM) and a prominent framework for generative artificial intelligence.

GatedRecurrentUnit.label: Gated Recurrent Unit
GatedRecurrentUnit.definition: The GRU is like a long short-term memory (LSTM) with a forget gate, but has fewer parameters than LSTM, as it lacks an output gate. GRU's performance on certain tasks of polyphonic music modeling, speech signal modeling and natural language processing was found to be similar to that of LSTM

GenerativeAdversarialNetwork.label: Generative Adversarial Network
GenerativeAdversarialNetwork.definition: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) are an approach to generative modeling using deep learning methods, such as convolutional neural networks.

GeometricMean.label: Geometric Mean
GeometricMean.definition: The nth root of the product of the data values, where there are n of these. This measure is valid only for data that are measured absolutely on a strictly positive scale.

GetSystemTime.label: Get System Time
GetSystemTime.definition: A system call that gets the system time.  For POSIX.1 systems, time() invokes a call to get the system time.

GlobalUserAccount.label: Global User Account
GlobalUserAccount.definition: A type of user account in Microsoft Windows (NT) that has a domain-wide scope.defines that user's access to a logical group of network objects (computers, users, devices) that share the same Active Directory databases; that is, a user's access to the domain.

GoodmanAndKruskalsGamma.label: Goodman and Kruskal's Gamma
GoodmanAndKruskalsGamma.definition: Goodman-Kruskal $\\gamma$ is a measure of rank correlation between x and y and is given by $(n_c -n_d) / (n_c + n_d)$, where $n_c$ is the number of concordant pairs of the observations and $n_d$ is the number of discordant pairs.

GradientBoostedDecisionTree.label: Gradient-Boosted Decision Tree
GradientBoostedDecisionTree.definition: A gradient-boosted decision tree is, as in other bagging and boosting methods, a method where the relatively 'weak' machine learning model (a decision tree) is used in an ensemble to form a 'strong' machine learning model.

Graph-basedClustering.label: Graph-based Clustering
Graph-basedClustering.definition: Graph-based Clustering is a form of clustering where data is represented with graphs to identify clusters.  We include Connection-based Clustering in this class.

Graph-basedSemi-supervisedLearning.label: Graph-based Semi-supervised Learning
Graph-basedSemi-supervisedLearning.definition: Graph-based Semi-Supervised Learning (GSSL) methods aim to classify unlabeled data by learning the graph structure and labeled data jointly.

GraphicalUserInterface.label: Graphical User Interface
GraphicalUserInterface.definition: A graphical user interface (GUI)  is a type of user interface that allows users to interact with electronic devices through graphical icons and visual indicators such as secondary notation, instead of text-based user interfaces, typed command labels or text navigation. GUIs were introduced in reaction to the perceived steep learning curve of command-line interfaces (CLIs), which require commands to be typed on a computer keyboard.

GraphicsCardFirmware.label: Graphics Card Firmware
GraphicsCardFirmware.definition: Firmware that is installed on computer graphics card.

GraphicsProcessingUnit.label: Graphics Processing Unit
GraphicsProcessingUnit.definition: A Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) is a specialized processor designed to efficiently perform parallel computations, primarily for rendering graphics and visual data.

Grid-CNN.label: Grid-CNN
Grid-CNN.definition: A class of neural networks that specializes in processing data that has a grid-like topology, such as an image.

Grid-basedClustering.label: Grid-based Clustering
Grid-basedClustering.definition: Divides the entire data space into a finite number of cells reducing the complexity of the data and focuses on the cells rather than the data.

GroupCreationEvent.label: Group Creation Event
GroupCreationEvent.definition: An event where a new group is established within the system, defining an entity to manage users and permissions collectively.

GroupDeletionEvent.label: Group Deletion Event
GroupDeletionEvent.definition: An event where an existing group is permanently removed from the system, dissolving its associated memberships and privileges.

GroupManagementEvent.label: Group Management Event
GroupManagementEvent.definition: An event involving the creation, modification, or deletion of a group, or changes to its membership and privileges. Group management events facilitate the enforcement of role-based access control by organizing users and permissions into logical units for streamlined administration and policy enforcement.

GroupPolicy.label: Group Policy
GroupPolicy.definition: Group Policy is a feature of the Microsoft Windows NT family of operating systems that controls the working environment of user accounts and computer accounts. Group Policy provides the centralized management and configuration of operating systems, applications, and users' settings in an Active Directory environment. A version of Group Policy called Local Group Policy ("LGPO" or "LocalGPO") also allows Group Policy Object management on standalone and non-domain computers.

HMIApplication.label: HMI Application
HMIApplication.definition: Application software which runs the main program in an HMI.

HMIApplicationProcess.label: HMI Application Process
HMIApplicationProcess.definition: The instructions within an HMI defined by user programming to interpret visual (and potentially audio) inputs and define visual (and potentially) audio outputs.

HTMLFile.label: HTML File
HTMLFile.definition: A document file encoded in HTML.The HyperText Markup Language, or HTML is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser. It can be assisted by technologies such as Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) and scripting languages such as JavaScript. Web browsers receive HTML documents from a web server or from local storage and render the documents into multimedia web pages. HTML describes the structure of a web page semantically and originally included cues for the appearance of the document.

HTTPConnectEvent.label: HTTP CONNECT Event
HTTPConnectEvent.definition: An event where the HTTP CONNECT method is used to establish a tunnel to the server identified by the target resource.

HTTPDeleteEvent.label: HTTP DELETE Event
HTTPDeleteEvent.definition: An event where the HTTP DELETE method is used to delete the specified resource.

HTTPEvent.label: HTTP Event
HTTPEvent.definition: An event involving the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), which operates over TCP to transmit hypermedia documents.

HTTPGetEvent.label: HTTP GET Event
HTTPGetEvent.definition: An event where the HTTP GET method is used to request a representation of the specified resource.

HTTPHeadEvent.label: HTTP HEAD Event
HTTPHeadEvent.definition: An event where the HTTP HEAD method is used to request metadata about the specified resource without the response body.

HTTPOptionsEvent.label: HTTP OPTIONS Event
HTTPOptionsEvent.definition: An event where the HTTP OPTIONS method is used to describe the communication options for the target resource.

HTTPPostEvent.label: HTTP POST Event
HTTPPostEvent.definition: An event where the HTTP POST method is used to submit data to the specified resource, often causing a change in state or side effects on the server.

HTTPPutEvent.label: HTTP PUT Event
HTTPPutEvent.definition: An event where the HTTP PUT method is used to replace all current representations of the target resource with the request payload.

HTTPRequestEvent.label: HTTP Request Event
HTTPRequestEvent.definition: An event where an HTTP request is sent from a client to a server over an established TCP connection.

HTTPResponseEvent.label: HTTP Response Event
HTTPResponseEvent.definition: An event where an HTTP response is sent from a server to a client over an established TCP connection.

HTTPTraceEvent.label: HTTP TRACE Event
HTTPTraceEvent.definition: An event where the HTTP TRACE method is used to perform a message loop-back test along the path to the target resource.

HardDiskFirmware.label: Hard Disk Firmware
HardDiskFirmware.definition: Firmware that is installed on a hard disk device.

HardLink.label: Hard Link
HardLink.definition: In computing, a hard link is a directory entry that associates a name with a file on a file system. All directory-based file systems must have at least one hard link giving the original name for each file. The term "hard link" is usually only used in file systems that allow more than one hard link for the same file. Multiple hard links -- that is, multiple directory entries to the same file -- are supported by POSIX-compliant and partially POSIX-compliant operating systems, such as Linux, Android, macOS, and also Windows NT4 and later Windows NT operating systems.

Harden.label: Harden
Harden.definition: The harden tactic is used to increase the opportunity cost of computer network exploitation. Hardening differs from Detection in that it generally is conducted before a system is online and operational.

HardeningEvent.label: Hardening Event
HardeningEvent.definition: An event involving actions to strengthen defenses, such as applying patches or implementing secure configurations, reducing attack surfaces, and increasing the difficulty of exploitation by adversaries.

Hardware-basedProcessIsolation.label: Hardware-based Process Isolation
Hardware-basedProcessIsolation.definition: Preventing one process from writing to the memory space of another process through hardware based address manager implementations.

Hardware-basedWriteProtection.label: Hardware-based Write Protection
Hardware-basedWriteProtection.definition: Physical methods of preventing data from being written to computer storage.

HardwareClock.label: Hardware Clock
HardwareClock.definition: A clock implemented using physical electronic components, typically providing timekeeping independent of system power or software state.

HardwareClockDeviceDriver.label: Hardware Clock Device Driver
HardwareClockDeviceDriver.definition: A device driver for a hardware clock.

HardwareClockEvent.label: Hardware Clock Event
HardwareClockEvent.definition: A clock event involving a physical timekeeping mechanism implemented in hardware components.

HardwareComponentInventory.label: Hardware Component Inventory
HardwareComponentInventory.definition: Hardware component inventorying identifies and records the hardware items in the organization's architecture.

HardwareDevice.label: Hardware Device
HardwareDevice.definition: Hardware devices are the physical artifacts that constitute a network or computer system. Hardware devices are the physical parts or components of a computer, such as the monitor, keyboard, computer data storage, hard disk drive (HDD), graphic cards, sound cards, memory (RAM), motherboard, and so on, all of which are tangible physical objects. By contrast, software is instructions that can be stored and run by hardware. Hardware is directed by the software to execute any command or instruction. A combination of hardware and software forms a usable computing system.

HardwareDeviceBindEvent.label: Hardware Device Bind Event
HardwareDeviceBindEvent.definition: An event where a device is logically bound to a system or process, typically for exclusive use or integration with specific software components.

HardwareDeviceConfiguration.label: Hardware Device Configuration
HardwareDeviceConfiguration.definition: Information used to configure the parameters and settings for hardware devices.

HardwareDeviceConnectionEvent.label: Hardware Device Connection Event
HardwareDeviceConnectionEvent.definition: An event representing the physical or logical attachment of a device to a system, enabling its operational functionality.

HardwareDeviceDisabledEvent.label: Hardware Device Disabled Event
HardwareDeviceDisabledEvent.definition: An event where a device transitions to an inactive or unavailable state, often due to deactivation, failure, or maintenance.

HardwareDeviceDisconnectionEvent.label: Hardware Device Disconnection Event
HardwareDeviceDisconnectionEvent.definition: An event representing the removal of a device from a system, ceasing its operational functionality or availability.

HardwareDeviceEnabledEvent.label: Hardware Device Enabled Event
HardwareDeviceEnabledEvent.definition: An event where a device becomes operational and available for use, typically following initialization, activation, or repair.

HardwareDeviceEvent.label: Hardware Device Event
HardwareDeviceEvent.definition: An event capturing the existence, state, or interaction of hardware or virtual devices within a system. Device events encompass activities such as discovery, connection, disconnection, operational state changes, or configuration modifications, providing visibility into device behavior and health.

HardwareDeviceMoveEvent.label: Hardware Device Move Event
HardwareDeviceMoveEvent.definition: An event where a device is relocated or reassigned within a system or network, potentially affecting its operational scope or connectivity.

HardwareDeviceStateEvent.label: Hardware Device State Event
HardwareDeviceStateEvent.definition: An event involving a change to a device's state, such as connection, disconnection, modification, or operational state transitions (e.g., online or offline). Device state events provide visibility into device availability and operational conditions.

HardwareDeviceUnbindEvent.label: Hardware Device Unbind Event
HardwareDeviceUnbindEvent.definition: An event where a device is logically unbound from a system or process, releasing it from exclusive use or integration.

HardwareDeviceUpdateEvent.label: Hardware Device Update Event
HardwareDeviceUpdateEvent.definition: An event capturing updates or changes to a device's configuration, properties, or state, including firmware updates, reconfigurations, or optimizations.

HardwareDriver.label: Hardware Driver
HardwareDriver.definition: In computing, a device driver (commonly referred to simply as a driver) is a computer program that operates or controls a particular type of device that is attached to a computer. A driver provides a software interface to hardware devices, enabling operating systems and other computer programs to access hardware functions without needing to know precise details of the hardware being used. A driver communicates with the device through the computer bus or communications subsystem to which the hardware connects. When a calling program invokes a routine in the driver, the driver issues commands to the device. Once the device sends data back to the driver, the driver may invoke routines in the original calling program. Drivers are hardware dependent and operating-system-specific. They usually provide the interrupt handling required for any necessary asynchronous time-dependent hardware interface.

HardwareTimer.label: Hardware Timer
HardwareTimer.definition: A hardware timer is defined as an electronic component that serves as an 8-bit or 16-bit counter, capable of measuring time intervals, generating timed outputs, and driving loads through mechanisms such as pulse width modulation (PWM).

HardwareTimerConfigurationEvent.label: Hardware Timer Configuration Event
HardwareTimerConfigurationEvent.definition: An event in which a hardware timer's registers or operational parameters are programmed or modified.

HardwareTimerDeviceDriver.label: Hardware Timer Device Driver
HardwareTimerDeviceDriver.definition: A device driver for a hardware timer.

HardwareTimerEvent.label: Hardware Timer Event
HardwareTimerEvent.definition: A timer event involving a physical timer mechanism implemented in hardware components.

HardwareTimerInterruptEvent.label: Hardware Timer Interrupt Event
HardwareTimerInterruptEvent.definition: An event in which a hardware timer generates an interrupt signal upon expiration or interval completion.

HardwareWatchdogTimer.label: Hardware Watchdog Timer
HardwareWatchdogTimer.definition: A hardware watchdog timer is a watchdog timer implemented using electronic components.

HarmonicMean.label: Harmonic Mean
HarmonicMean.definition: The reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of the reciprocals of the data values. This measure too is valid only for data that are measured absolutely on a strictly positive scale.

HeapSegment.label: Heap Segment
HeapSegment.definition: The heap segment (or free store) is a large pool of memory from which dynamic memory requests of a process are allocated and satisfied.

HeterogeneousAsymmetricFeature-basedTran.label: Heterogeneous Asymmetric Feature-based Transfer Learning
HeterogeneousAsymmetricFeature-basedTran.definition: Asymmetric transformation mapping  transforms the source feature space to align with that of the target or the target to that of the source. This, in effect, bridges the feature space gap and reduces the problem into a homogeneous transfer problem when further distribution differences need to be corrected.

HeterogeneousFeature-basedTransferLearni.label: Heterogeneous Feature-based Transfer Learning
HeterogeneousFeature-basedTransferLearni.definition: Symmetric transformation  takes both the source feature space Xs and target feature space Xt and learns feature transformations as to project each onto a common subspace Xc for adaptation purposes. This derived subspace becomes a domain-invariant feature subspace to associate cross-domain data, and in effect, reduces marginal distribution differences.

HeterogeneousTransferLearning.label: Heterogeneous Transfer Learning
HeterogeneousTransferLearning.definition: Heterogeneous transfer learning is characterized by the source and target domains having differing feature spaces, but may also be combined with other issues such as differing data distributions and label spaces.

HierarchicalClustering.label: Hierarchical Clustering
HierarchicalClustering.definition: Hierarchical clustering (also called hierarchical cluster analysis or HCA) is a method of cluster analysis that seeks to build a hierarchy of clusters.

HierarchicalDomainDenylisting.label: Hierarchical Domain Denylisting
HierarchicalDomainDenylisting.definition: Blocking the resolution of any subdomain of a specified domain name.

High-dimensionClustering.label: High-dimension Clustering
High-dimensionClustering.definition: The cluster analysis of data with anywhere from a few dozen to many thousands of dimensions.

Higher-orderLogic.label: Higher-order Logic
Higher-orderLogic.definition: Higher-order logic is a form of predicate logic that is distinguished from first-order logic by additional quantifiers and, sometimes, stronger semantics. Higher-order logics with their standard semantics are more expressive, but their model-theoretic properties are less well-behaved than those of first-order logic.

HomogenousTransferLearning.label: Homogenous Transfer Learning
HomogenousTransferLearning.definition: In homogeneous transfer learning, the feature spaces of the source and target domains is of the same dimension (Ds = Dt) while the data of both domains is represented by the same attributes (Xs = Xt) and labels (Ys = Yt). Thus, homogeneous transfer learning aims to bridge the gap in the data distributions experienced during cross-domain transfer.

HomoglyphDenylisting.label: Homoglyph Denylisting
HomoglyphDenylisting.definition: Blocking DNS queries that are deceptively similar to legitimate domain names.

HomoglyphDetection.label: Homoglyph Detection
HomoglyphDetection.definition: Comparing strings using a variety of techniques to determine if a deceptive or malicious string is being presented to a user.
